ShortDescription.Value: DEV TEST BUILD of Traffic: Clear the Way. Unstable - do not use on a city you care about.

Publish.LongDescription:
⚠️ **This is the development build of _Traffic: Clear the Way_. It is not the mod you want.**
Install the normal release instead - this page exists so testers can try changes before they ship.
- Expect rough edges: unfinished behaviour, debug logging, values that change between uploads. - Do **not** run it on a city you care about. Keep a backup save. - Never run it alongside the release version - both register the same systems.
Feedback on a dev build is most useful with `Logs/ClearTheWay.log` attached (switch on "Verbose logging" in the options first).
Release version: https://mods.paradoxplaza.com/mods/151583/Windows
Publish.ChangeLog:
0.1.12.1 - performance.
The simulation runs measurably faster with this build. Measured against the public release on the same city at the same load: **+14% simulation tick rate**, and the busier it gets the more it helps - at 50+ emergency vehicles running at once it was +19%. Over a 3.5-hour session, with no drift: the tick rate in the last twenty minutes was the same as in the first.
**Where it came from** All of it is the pedestrian pass - the one that holds people at the kerb while a responder passes. It turned out to cost about 10% of every simulation tick on its own, and now costs almost nothing.
- It searched a cube of 40 m in every direction around each siren - including 40 m backwards, and 40 m up and down. On a map with tunnels or elevated roads that dragged whole extra layers of footpath into the search, all of it thrown away again a moment later. It now looks only along the stretch the responder is actually driving. - The check "has this responder already passed you?" used to run ninth, after eight component lookups. It runs first now. - The full search runs every 10 simulation ticks instead of every 4. Pedestrians already held stay held on every tick as before - only the moment a NEW one is noticed shifts, by about 0.2 seconds.
**What that means for behaviour** Practically nothing should look different. If anything does, it would be a pedestrian stepping off a kerb that would previously have waited - most likely at a wide junction while a responder is turning. That is the one case where the smaller search box gives up coverage, and it is the thing worth reporting.
**Everything below was already in the previous dev build**
**Worth knowing before you start** - Cars are allowed onto flat medians, grass strips and empty tram beds to clear the way. That is deliberate and switchable ("Cross medians"), not a bug. - Never run this alongside the public release.
**Towing** - Wrecks get hauled away and delivered instead of the truck giving up halfway. - A recovery truck that is merely queueing in traffic is no longer "rescued" every 15 seconds. It used to be teleported back onto the lane it was already standing on, forever - 904 no-op recoveries in one 100-minute session - and doing so rewrote lane fields behind the game's back, which can take the whole simulation down. - A truck that is genuinely off the network, or has not moved for ~5 minutes, is removed and its wreck goes back into the queue. Losing one truck beats an unstable save.
**Emergency corridor** - A responder squeezing past two cars abreast could stall completely: the game only ever ignores ONE blocker, and with two stopped cars the blocker flipped every tick so neither was ignored. It now noses out of that state on its own. - Cars are pulled aside by an amount that matches the room actually beside THEIR side of the road. On carriageways running against the road direction the mod measured the far side and handed out up to 4 m of space that was not there, which is what threw cars across parking bays and onto kerbs.
**What to report** Log with "Verbose logging" enabled, plus roughly where it happened. Responders that stand still, cars ending up somewhere they physically should not be, and anything that stutters are all interesting.
